plan.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) months 2–6: what to expect after the first month, organised by experience (appetite, how stomach side effects tend to change, the shape of average weight change, hair shedding, the oral-contraceptive note around dose increases, injection-site reactions), using only the US Zepbound label (rev. 28 Aug 2026) and SURMOUNT-1 (NEJM 2022). Playbook queue #5, the sequel to First Month.
plan.angle: Tirzepatide after the first month: what usually changes, organised by experience and drawn only from the US Zepbound label (rev. 28 Aug 2026), SURMOUNT-1 (NEJM 2022) and the Mounjaro label (rev. 27 Aug 2026) for any shared statement. If the Mounjaro label isn't used, retitle to 'Tirzepatide (Zepbound) After Month 1: What to Expect' and leave Mounjaro out of all packaging. Use 'months two to six' only as the viewer's frame, and never tie an effect to a specific month. Line for the 15 s payoff: 'stomach side effects happened mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time, and in SURMOUNT-1 average weight kept going down for many months.' Second payoff: nausea as a by-dose range versus placebo (no mg figures spoken or shown), with the label's pooled-trial population copied exactly from section 6.1. Keep every other chapter, safety line and structural rule as briefed: appetite in label wording, the hedged 'food noise' framing, the 72-week SURMOUNT-1 average with its full population ('averages, not predictions'), hair 5.4% vs 0.9% (women 7.1%, men 0.5%), and oral hormonal contraceptives 'for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase' with no increase schedule. Injection-site reactions are 6–8% by dose vs about 2% on placebo, with the rotation tip credited to the IFU or paraphrased from the label. Protein comes with a kidney caveat, and strength training 2+ days a week is marked 'recommended'. Include the diabetes-plus-insulin/sulfonylurea low-blood-sugar line and the severe-stomach-pain emergency line, followed by the scoped don't-switch/stop/change line. No dose numbers, and the 'Not personal advice' and prescriber lines are both spoken and shown on screen.
plan.why:
This is the next ready item in the playbook queue (#5) and a search-demand timeline that completes the First Month series. Every fact comes from the label and SURMOUNT-1, already verified, so it should pass the fact-check first time. Confirm the 11-16 plan never went live before rendering. | fact-check: Good evergreen sequel to First Month. It's on-pillar and has real search demand, and the brief already fixes most of the known failure modes: label wording for GI effects, the hair-loss figures, the injection-site figures, oral contraceptives only, the low-blood-sugar scope, the emergency line and no dosing calendar. Four things need fixing before scripting.
(1) Mounjaro scope: the working title and the topic both name Mounjaro, but the only sources listed are the Zepbound label and SURMOUNT-1. The house rule says a Mounjaro keyword needs Mounjaro's own label (PI rev 27 Aug 2026). Either cite it for the shared sections (contraceptive interaction, GI, injection site) or drop 'Mounjaro' from the title and hashtags. Keep in mind that Mounjaro's figures come from type 2 diabetes trials, so never mix its numbers with Zepbound's.
(2) Internal conflict: the brief asks for 'one pooled nausea rate per dose' but also 'no dose numbers'. Give the rate as a by-dose range ('about X to Y in 100, depending on dose, versus about Z in 100 on placebo'), copied from Zepbound section 6.1, and name the label's pooled-trial population exactly as printed. Don't call it SURMOUNT-1 only, and don't add or drop 'with or without type 2 diabetes'. Read the pool definition in the label and don't assume it.
(3) Timeline framing: neither source reports outcomes by month 2, 3 and so on. 'Months 2–6' can be the viewer's frame, but the script must not attach any effect to a specific month. Hair shedding has no timing in the label, and weight change is described over 72 weeks. The 15 s payoff should say 'in SURMOUNT-1', not 'in the trials', and the wording should be 'average weight kept going down for many months', with no plateau week read off the graph.
(4) The contraceptive chapter should say 'after starting and after each dose increase' without saying how often increases happen. That keeps any titration calendar out.
Other notes: the brief's spoken closing line is fine, but the description watch-next line is added by the publisher (target: Side Effects). Mention it only in post notes and don't type it into the description.

package.description:
Call your prescriber right away, or get emergency help, if you have severe stomach pain that won't go away, with or without vomiting. Call your local emergency number right away if your face, lips, tongue or throat swell, or you have trouble breathing. For anything that isn't one of those emergency signs, don't stop, switch or change your medicine on your own. This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice.

Quick answer: on the Zepbound label, most nausea, vomiting and diarrhea happened during dose escalation and decreased over time. In SURMOUNT-1, average weight on tirzepatide kept going down for many months.

scenes.narration: Dose escalation means the planned steps up your prescriber makes. When and how is between you and them, so this video leaves it out.
So if a stretch after a step up feels rougher than a steady stretch, that fits the label's pattern. It's a pattern, though, not a promise.

scenes.narration: Besides nausea, the label's common stomach reactions include diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, belly pain and indigestion.
Burping and acid reflux are on that list too.
In SURMOUNT one, most of these stomach events were mild to moderate, and they happened mainly during dose escalation.
And here's a number that puts it in perspective. About four to seven in a hundred people on tirzepatide stopped because of adverse events, depending on dose.

scenes.narration: One more thing the label flags. Losing fluid through vomiting or diarrhea can lead to dehydration, and that's been linked to kidney problems.
So sip fluids through the day, unless you've been told to limit fluids.

scenes.narration: So what did weight change look like in the big tirzepatide weight trial?

In SURMOUNT one, adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes, lost an average of about fifteen to twenty-one percent of body weight by seventy-two weeks, depending on dose.

factcheck.summary:
I checked the main numbers and found no errors. Two sources were checked directly: the SURMOUNT-1 abstract (through Europe PMC, because PubMed blocked the fetch) and the Zepbound label text (through a search result, because the PDFs return as unreadable binary).

SURMOUNT-1 matches the script:
- Weight change at 72 weeks: −15.0%, −19.5% and −20.9% by dose, vs −3.1% on placebo.
- Lost at least 5%: 85%, 89% and 91%, vs 35% on placebo.
- Stopped because of adverse events: 4.3%, 7.1% and 6.2%, vs 2.6% on placebo.
- Stomach events: "most were mild to moderate… occurring primarily during dose escalation".

The Zepbound label confirms:
- Nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea happened mostly during dose escalation and decreased over time.
- Nausea was 28% on the 15 mg dose vs 8% on placebo.
- Hair loss was 7.1% in women vs 0.5% in men on Zepbound, compared with 1.3% vs 0% on placebo.

The other figures match the known label values in the craft notes rather than being re-read here: nausea 25–29% by dose, injection-site reactions 6–8% vs about 2%, and hair loss 5.4% vs 0.9%. The birth-control, calorie-intake, site-rotation, kidney, low-blood-sugar and boxed-warning lines match standard label wording. The PAG 2+ days a week for muscle strengthening is accurate.

Both label PDFs and the HHS guideline PDF load, though none could be read as text; the revision dates (Zepbound 28 Aug 2026, Mounjaro 27 Aug 2026) match the known dates. The PubMed link is a real record; the fetch was blocked by cookies.

The safety lines are complete:
- the scoped don't-stop line
- severe stomach pain to call about right away
- the emergency line for swelling or trouble breathing
- the fluid caveat
- the kidney-disease protein caveat
- low blood sugar limited to type 2 diabetes plus insulin or a sulfonylurea
- the MTC/MEN 2 boxed warning
- the prescriber line

Priya is clearly hypothetical. A subscribe line and "linked in the description" are allowed in long-form. There are only minor fixes, all on muted-viewer clarity and the hair comparator.

The automatic cue pass left about 18 spikes where a pop/swoosh/bubble/swell briefly jumped to -3 to -11dB under spoken lines (loud transitions landing mid-sentence); those are pulled back to -16 to -17dB so they're felt, not heard, while leaving the many well-placed -14 to -18dB cues untouched. Kept SFX density as-is elsewhere since no second shows more than 3-4 simultaneous hits. Added five light, medically-safe custom accents (a playful stomach-rumble for the appetite beat, a reassuring chime for the injection-site headline, an airy hair-swish, and two hushed low tones for the severe-pain and boxed-warning moments) to add texture to serious beats without any injection/pill-adjacent sound.

issues: 72-week SURMOUNT-1 trial span doesn't clearly match the video's 'Months 2-6' personal-experience framing, slight promise mismatch
generic silhouette+question mark could apply to almost any topic, weaker specific pull than #0

thumbnail.reasoning: All three are legible at phone size with short, clean lines and no clutter. #0 ('STILL QUEASY? AFTER MONTH ONE') names the single biggest lingering worry for someone past month one — whether nausea persists — which directly matches the video's 'what to expect in months 2-6' promise and the worried stomach-mascot face matches the anxious tone of the text (no contradiction). It creates a sharp, specific curiosity gap without giving away the answer. #2 ('WHAT CHANGES NEXT?') is legible and on-brand with the sequel framing but is generic/abstract — a silhouette and question mark could headline almost any video, giving it less distinctive pull. #1 ('72 WEEKS / WHAT THE TRIAL SHOWED') is a credible, specific number, but it points to the SURMOUNT-1 trial timeline rather than the video's actual 'months 2-6 personal experience' framing, risking a mismatch between what's promised and what's delivered. None of the hard caps apply (no answer given away, no face/text contradiction, no title-word repetition), so the pick comes down to strongest honest curiosity pull, which is #0.

issues.problem: It doesn't name the drug. The script's on-screen card says "SURMOUNT-1, tirzepatide", so someone reading the description alone could miss that this is the tirzepatide arm. This is wording polish, not misleading. The fix adds only about 15 characters, so the description stays under 1,250.
issues.fix: In SURMOUNT-1, average weight on tirzepatide kept going down for many months.
